**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, December 12, 2023, Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called it to order at 7:00 p.m.; Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt and Wilson were present, Dr. Philippart absent. Superintendent Machesky attended with administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Hall, Zawislak and West, before an audience of approximately 60. Adjournment 9:42 p.m.; minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.

**Recognitions**
- Silver Hornets, the Boulan Park Middle School robotics team of eight students, promoted to States at the recent District Championship and winners of the FIRST Inspire Award and FIRST Alliance Award. Coach Nivedita Maringanti introduced Ananya Siranjeevi, Sree Dhruthi Maringanti, Maanya Gupta, Aarush Arora, Sai Sathvik Reddy Thumma, Diya Siranjeevi, Mihir Kandage and Samarth Yadav.
- WEB ("Where Everybody Belongs") teacher leaders Philip Lewan, Allyson Pagnani, Emily Stetson, Judy Morgan, Maria Mendola, Jaclynn Parker, Cortney Walls and Raymond Torres.
- The Communications Department, recipient of a 2023 Michigan School Public Relations Association (MSPRA) Gold Medallion Award for Troy Bond 2022, Preparing for Tomorrow, plus MSPRA Excellence Awards: Social Media (Excellence), Audio/Podcast (Excellence), Financial Report, Website/Mobile App, Video, Newsletter and Marketing Materials (Merit). Rebecca Fannon presented awards to Kerry Birmingham, Melissa Verduyn, Patrice Rowbal, Thomas Butcher, Adam Burns and Linda Alfonso.
- Student Spotlight: Brianna Johnson, a senior at Athens High School, in the Creative Guild; Thomas Butcher, Creative Content Producer, described her work.

**Public communication (agenda items)**
Michele Maleszyk (ELA, data transparency, LTRS training), Dr. Audra Melton (dyslexia, Reading Recovery; gave each member the book Language at the Speed of Sight), Stephanie Zendler (achievement gap, students with disabilities), Tracy Owens (November workshop's combined single graph called misleading; asked for M-Step data broken down) and Suril Patel (lack of data supporting instruction) spoke. Additions and deletions: none.

**Consent agenda (moved Hauff, supported Haupt; items A-I)**
Minutes of the October 3, 2023 workshop; October 17, 2023 meeting; November 14, 2023 special meeting and closed session; November 14, 2023 workshop; second reading and adoption of revised/recommended Board policies; clergy member for the 2023-24 Sex Education Advisory Board; Treasurer's Reports for September 2023 and October 2023; General Fund Budget Amendment #1.

**Personnel**
A two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure was issued to Mr. Troy Wissink as Technology Director beginning January 1, 2024 (moved Anne, supported Wilson). Personnel recommendations for Sana Mirza and Sara Ranucci were approved (moved Alic, supported Anne).

**Business awards**

| Item | Vendor | Amount | Fund |
|---|---|---|---|
| iPads and cases | Apple Computers | $699,110.00 | 2023 Capital Projects |
| Smith Middle School electrical pre-purchase | Great Lakes Power and Lighting | not to exceed $279,900.00 | 2023 Capital Projects |
| Roof replacement | JD Candler (Services Building) $59,900.00; Royal West Roofing (Bemis, Transportation) $289,000.00; Quality Roofing (Morse, Wattles) $818,420.00; Contingency (5%) $58,366.00 | TOTAL $1,225,686.00 | 2023 Capital Projects |
| Site Work Paving Program | Nagle Paving Company | $1,758,370.00 | 2023 Capital Projects |
| Sitework projects (retention pond) | Eagle Excavation | $381,776.00 | Building Site and Sinking Fund |
| Walk-in cooler/freezer, Boulan Park and Larson | Stafford Smith | $227,606.32 | Food Service |

**Other**
DiPilato and Griffor presented assessment data covering SAT, PSAT, MSTEP, Fountas & Pinnell, Common Lit and NWEA-Math, with Oakland County and state comparisons. Sarah Krieger spoke during non-agenda communication about Mr. Schmidt's presentation in a Troy High Criminal Law class. Student representatives Teagan Pruitt, Nurayda Albeez, Jayla Turner and Marlien William reported. Schmidt announced a January 9, 2024 workshop at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building and the Organizational and Regular Board Meeting January 16 at 7:00 p.m. All recorded votes were 6 yes, 0 no, with Philippart absent.
2024_207_m121223bdmtg.verbose:
Minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held December 12, 2023 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt and Wilson were present; Dr. Philippart was absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Hall, Zawislak and West, with approximately 60 members of the audience. The minutes carry the notation GH/jh and were submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.

RECOGNITION - TSD MISSION MOMENT: SILVER HORNETS ROBOTICS. The Board recognized the Boulan Park Middle School Robotics Team, the Silver Hornets. The team of eight students built a robot able to perform certain tasks and functions and won awards in the FIRST Tech Challenge Robotics competition in 2022; the team had just been promoted to States in the recent District Championship competition and received the FIRST Inspire Award and the FIRST Alliance Award. Coach Nivedita Maringanti introduced Ananya Siranjeevi, Sree Dhruthi Maringanti, Maanya Gupta, Aarush Arora, Sai Sathvik Reddy Thumma, Diya Siranjeevi, Mihir Kandage and Samarth Yadav, who spoke about their project and demonstrated the robot for the Board and the Troy community.

RECOGNITION - TSD MISSION MOMENT: WEB TEACHER LEADERS. The Board recognized the WEB teacher leaders. WEB, which stands for "Where Everybody Belongs," is a middle school orientation and transition program that welcomes 6th graders through their first year of middle school. Built on the belief that students can help students succeed, it trains 8th grade mentors as WEB Leaders who guide 6th graders in the transition. WEB also functions as an anti-bullying program by providing a cadre of student leaders who look for bullying behavior and help stop it, creating a safer school environment. Philip Lewan, Allyson Pagnani, Emily Stetson, Judy Morgan, Maria Mendola, Jaclynn Parker, Cortney Walls and Raymond Torres were invited to the podium to share remarks.

RECOGNITION - MICHIGAN SCHOOL PUBLIC RELATIONS ASSOCIATION (MSPRA) AWARDS. The Board recognized the Troy School District Communications Department. The Communications team received a 2023 MSPRA Gold Medallion Award for Troy Bond 2022, Preparing for Tomorrow. The team was also recognized by the 2023 MSPRA Excellence Awards program with the following additional awards: Social Media - Excellence; Audio/Podcast - Excellence; Financial Report - Merit; Website/Mobile App - Merit; Video - Merit; Newsletter - Merit; Marketing Materials - Merit. Staff congratulated and presented with an award by Rebecca Fannon, the Membership & Marketing Co-Chair for MSPRA and the Public Relations and Marketing Coordinator for the West Bloomfield School District, were Kerry Birmingham, Melissa Verduyn, Patrice Rowbal, Thomas Butcher, Adam Burns and Linda Alfonso.

STUDENT SPOTLIGHT. The Student Spotlight recognizes the talents and achievements of students in the Creative Guild. The Board recognized Brianna Johnson, a senior at Athens High School; Thomas Butcher, Creative Content Producer from the TSD Creative Guild, described her work.

ADDITIONS & DELETIONS. None.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (AGENDA ITEMS). Ms. Michele Maleszyk, Troy resident and parent in District, addressed the Board about ELA, student achievement data transparency and LTRS training for teachers, and provided packets with student achievement data. Dr. Audra Melton, retired TSD administrator and parent in District, addressed dyslexia, Reading Recovery and District achievement data, and provided the book Language at the Speed of Sight to each board member. Mrs. Stephanie Zendler, former TSD administrator and parent in District, addressed student achievement data, students with disabilities and the achievement gap, and commented that the current ELA program is ineffective. Mrs. Tracy Owens, TSD parent, addressed the District's ELA curriculum and commented that the data provided at the November workshop was combined into a single graph, which is misleading, saying it would be helpful to have the M-Step data broken down. Mr. Suril Patel, a property owner who will move to Troy soon, addressed the lack of data to support what is being taught and shortcomings of Troy with data collection.

GENERAL - CONSENT AGENDA. It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H and I on the consent agenda: Minutes of the October 3, 2023 Board of Education Workshop; Minutes of the October 17, 2023 Board of Education Meeting; Minutes of the November 14, 2023 Special Board of Education Meeting & Closed Session; Minutes of the November 14, 2023 Board of Education Workshop; Second Reading and Adoption - Revised/Recommended Board Policies; Clergy Member for 2023-24 Sex Education Advisory Board; Treasurer's Report - September 2023; Treasurer's Report - October 2023; General Fund Budget Amendment #1. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

PERSONNEL - ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, TECHNOLOGY DIRECTOR. It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Wilson that the Board of Education issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. Troy Wissink, who will begin his duties as Technology Director as of January 1, 2024. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

PERSONNEL - ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY. It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne that the Board approve the personnel recommendations as stated: Sana Mirza, Sara Ranucci. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

CURRICULUM - STUDENT ACHIEVEMENT DATA. Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction Christine DiPilato and Assistant Superintendent of Elementary Instruction Kris Griffor gave a PowerPoint presentation on student assessment data, reviewing SAT, PSAT and MSTEP results plus instructional and benchmarking data such as Fountas & Pinnell, Common Lit, NWEA - Math, exit data for advanced placement assessments and graduation rates. They provided comparisons with other districts in Oakland County and the state of Michigan and reviewed reading, writing and math scores. Celebrations shared included the International Baccalaureate Diploma Program, the International Academy East IB diploma acquisition rate, Advanced Placement courses, AP Honor Roll status for Athens and Troy High, and graduation rates for Troy College and Career High School. The Board discussed learning lost during Covid and supports in place for credit recovery.

BUSINESS - iPAD PURCHASE (BOND). It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic that the district purchase iPads and cases from Apple Computers in the amount of $699,110.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Funds. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

BUSINESS - SMITH ELECTRICAL GEAR PRE-PURCHASE (BOND). It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mr. Hauff that the bid for the pre-purchase of electrical equipment for Smith Middle School be awarded to Great Lakes Power and Lighting in an amount not to exceed $279,900.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

BUSINESS - ROOFING PROJECTS (BOND). It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Wilson that the bid for roof replacement be awarded as follows, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund: JD Candler, Services Building, $59,900.00; Royal West Roofing, Bemis and Transportation, $289,000.00; Quality Roofing, Morse and Wattles, $818,420.00; Contingency (5%), $58,366.00; TOTAL $1,225,686.00. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

BUSINESS - PAVEMENT REPLACEMENT PROJECTS. It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Alic that the bid for the Site Work Paving Program be awarded to Nagle Paving Company in the amount of $1,758,370.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

BUSINESS - RETENTION POND RENOVATION PROJECT. It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt that the bid for sitework projects be awarded to Eagle Excavation in the amount of $381,776.00, approved as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

BUSINESS - FOOD SERVICE, BOULAN & LARSON EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT. It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mr. Hauff that the removal and replacement of the existing walk-in cooler and freezer at both Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools be awarded to Stafford Smith in the amount of $227,606.32, approved as an expenditure of the Food Service Fund. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (NON-AGENDA ITEMS). Mrs. Sarah Krieger, Troy resident and parent of students in the District, addressed the Board about Mr. Schmidt's presentation in her children's Criminal Law class at Troy High School and about bringing politics into the classroom.

OTHER - REPORTS FROM STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES TO THE BOARD. Teagan Pruitt (Troy College and Career High School), Nurayda Albeez (International Academy-East), Jayla Turner (Troy High School) and Marlien William (Athens High School) each reported on events and activities at their schools.

BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS. Board members wished everyone happy holidays. Mr. Haupt announced that Teacher of the Year nominations are being accepted and encouraged parents to nominate a teacher. Mrs. Anne shared that Ms. Griffor and the ELA team helped her understand how reading and writing are taught and that the district has many tools at its disposal, including phonics and pictures, with teachers teaching to their students' needs. Mr. Hauff attended the Baker Orchestra and Choir Concert and described the fine arts program as thriving. Dr. Wilson thanked Mr. Haupt and Mrs. Alic for completing their first year on the board and mentioned the recent MASB Conference. Dr. Machesky congratulated the fine arts teachers for the numerous holiday concerts, recognized the SSAB Executive Board for planning the District's annual MLK Day event, noted that donations of fleece are desperately needed for that event, and said there would also be a blood drive and other community activities; he also reported that Oakland Schools' STEMI mobile innovation lab was located in the Services Building parking lot, where students can visit for 45-minute sessions. Mr. Schmidt discussed the preservation of Section 1 and the trust fund grant applied for with Oakland County Parks and Six Rivers Conservancy, and announced that the next Board Workshop would be held January 9, 2024 at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building and the Organizational and Regular Board Meeting on Tuesday, January 16 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building.

ADJOURNMENT. The meeting adjourned at 9:42 p.m.
